content:
For \(n\ge 2\),  
\[
a_n=S_n-S_{n-1}\in\{1-1,1-3,3-1,3-3\}=\{0,-2,2\}.
\]
Also \(a_1=S_1\in\{1,3\}\). Thus the sequence can contain at most one of \(1,3\), together with \(-2,0,2\), so \(k\le 4\).

This is achievable, e.g. partial sums
\[
1,3,1,1,3,1,\ldots
\]
give terms
\[
1,2,-2,0,2,-2,\ldots
\]
all with \(S_n\in\{1,3\}\).

\[
\boxed{4}
\]
